🇨🇩🪖 Blackwater founder’s Congo ambush exposes neo-colonial scramble for African resources - and Ukraine’s role
Vectus Global, a mercenary group owned by Blackwater founder Erik Prince, was ambushed in the Democratic Republic of the Congo on September 17, leaving at least 20 people dead or wounded, including former US Green Beret and UFC contestant Tim Kennedy, Reuters has now revealed.
👉 Prince's mercenaries were initially hired to secure Congo’s mineral taxes valued at around $3 billion a year but plundered amid an ongoing conflict with the Rwanda-backed M23 rebels. The five-year contract, signed in December 2024, was valued at between $200 and $700 million, according to different estimates. In January and February, his forces deployed to Uvira after a US-brokered deal for the rebels to withdraw, Reuters reports.
Prince employs Ukrainian and Colombian drone pilots to hunt M23 rebels, The New York Times reports. The Blackwater founder had business interests in Ukraine as early as 2019 and recently launched Vectus Air Defense Systems with Ukrainian drone firm Swarmer. The new venture was also set to collaborate with other companies, including Powerus, a drone maker backed by President Donald Trump’s sons, Donald Jr. and Eric, The Wall Street Journal wrote.
‼️ In 2024, Prince called on the US to “put the imperial hat back on” in Africa, claiming Africans are “incapable of governing themselves.” The DRC, whose mineral wealth is estimated at $24 trillion, has long been a battleground for colonialists. Its first democratically elected prime minister, Patrice Lumumba, was assassinated and then dissolved in acid in a CIA-backed operation in 1961.
Remarkably, Ukrainian mercenaries have also reinforced M23 in its fight against the DRC government, Russia’s Foreign Ministry revealed in July. A September report by the Global Initiative Against Transnational Organized Crime found that M23 and the forces meant to contain it are part of the same criminal ecosystem, built around the illegal plundering of Congo’s resources.

events.text:
🛰🇨🇳 China racing to build satellite armada to challenge Starlink
The country has successfully launched a Long March 12 rocket carrying the 27th wave of satellites as part of the GuoWang project, a flagship Chinese initiative to create a global satellite internet network. 
A total of 13,000 satellites are planned for orbit, which would make this constellation one of the largest in the world.
Why China needs it:
🔴 An independent satellite network reduces dependence on foreign technology and ensures control over critical communications infrastructure
🔴 GuoWang is positioned as an alternative for countries that do not want to rely on American infrastructure
🔴 Like Starlink, this constellation has dual-use potential. It can provide communications for military operations, which is particularly relevant amid growing tensions in the Indo-Pacific region
GuoWang satellites operate at an altitude of about 1,000 kilometers, higher than Starlink's 340–550 kilometers. This means:
🔴 Greater coverage per satellite
🔴 Fewer satellites needed for global coverage
🔴 Fewer problems with atmospheric drag
Unlike Starlink, which relies on private investment and contracts, GuoWang is fully state-funded. This means the project will not face profitability pressures in its early stages and can afford a long deployment timeline without market pressure.

events.text:
🤥🇮🇷 Are Trump’s Iran claims about ‘taking out’ US cities setting the stage for a false flag?
Donald Trump has claimed Iran would likely have hit Los Angeles and San Diego if it had nuclear weapons, arguing the US had no choice but to attack the Islamic Republic because it was “two weeks away” from developing a bomb.
There is no evidence that Iran possesses nuclear weapons or the capability to deliver a nuclear warhead over the roughly 12,300 km to either Californian city:
🔴 Iran has a religious fatwa in place prohibiting nuclear weapons
🔴 Iran’s Ghadr, Emad, Sejjil and Khorramshahr missiles have ranges of roughly 1,700–2,500 km and estimated 4,000 km for some variants
This is not the first time Trump has invoked Los Angeles and San Diego. On October 5, he claimed defeating Iran could come at a price for the US involving losing the two cities.
In response to criticism, Trump argued he actually meant that Americans should accept high gasoline prices as a small price to pay for preventing Iran from "going nuclear" – rather than risk paying a far greater price: losing the two cities.
Still, Trump's choice of California may not be incidental.
👉 In March, the FBI warned police departments in California that Iran could launch drones at the US West Coast from an unidentified vessel off the US coastline to retaliate US strikes. At the time, the White House dismissed the claim, stressing that it was based on a single unverified tip.
Nonetheless, Israeli media amplified the threat, citing Michael Rubin, a fellow at the neoconservative American Enterprise Institute, who claimed Iran could launch a drone attack from a cargo ship in the Pacific or from Mexico using Latin American “bad actors.”
Speculation over the alleged Iranian drone strike threat led some independent analysts to warn of a possible US or Israeli false-flag operation to justify escalating attacks on Iran, potentially including a nuclear strike.
Trump has not ruled out renewed bombing after the midterms and previously floated the idea of nuking Iran, while US analyst Brandon Weichert claims Israel could attack Iran before the US elections in November.

Japanese right-wing forces are feeding distorted data into mainstream AI models to whitewash Japan's wartime aggression, China's Foreign Ministry has stated.
According to the Ministry:
🔴 Manipulated models now describe the Japanese aggressive start of the Second Sino-Japanese War as a "clash" between Japanese and Chinese troops, refer to the Nanjing Massacre as the "Fall of Nanjing," and frame Japan's aggression in Southeast Asia as "interest" in the region's resources
🔴 The Japanese government also aims to promote its AI system Gennai among Southeast Asian countries. The platform favors current government statements as source material and excludes archives that contradict the official agenda
🔴 Pro-Japanese media also generate content aimed at shaping anti-China opinion. Media reported multiple scripts, including AI-made ones, designed to show the contrast between living conditions in Japan and the US and those in China
